cultural.vision_reason: Engraved walrus-ivory bow drill depicting hunting scenes (walrus hunting, kayaks, tents) — a classic Iñupiaq/Alaskan Inuit tool and utensil, consistent with the claimed culture and category.

physical.title: bow drill
physical.summary: Drill bow made of walrus ivory, rectangular cross section, slightly curved, pierced at either end, for the skin cord, either missing or partially present with fragmentary cord registered with this item. Engraved on all four sides with scenes: a] left to right of walrus hunting: man and basking or surfacing walrus, massed walrus, man throwing harpoon from kayak at walrus; man about to throw harpoon from walrus, walrus with harpoon line and float attached, four kayaks with dead seal, or female walrus, last with harpooned walrus on its back; surfacing walrus, and three further kayaks and an unidentified boat. b] man firing an arrow at a goose, the goose alreday with an arrow [?] sticking out of its back; a canine looking at a kettle with a handle next to a harpoon stuck in the ground; an unfinished animal. c] two sod houses with figures, arrow pointing out of second house; series of sticks or harpoons stuck in ground; two further sode houses, the first with two people on top, second with a tethered dog on top, and a stretched skin [?]; three further sod structures; four umiaks stored on racks, the whaling harpoons above, and harpoon lines and toggles [?] dangling down. d] a caribou.
